newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Bouncy Belgian OLOs ogle EMU optimism.
newsitem.headline: Bouncy Belgian OLOs ogle EMU optimism.

text.p: Belgian government bonds (OLOs) and futures are looking for confirmation on fronts such as the future of EMU and U.S. interest rates, but dealers said on Friday only an upset would spark a significant reaction.
"The market set a direction for itself...a lot has been discounted already," a trader said.

Prices were slightly weaker at the end of Friday morning as players consolidated gains before U.S. PPI data due at 1230 GMT, forecast to confirm the benign trend gleaned from Thursday's retail sales data, and next week's Amsterdam summit by EU leaders, expected to ratify the post-euro stability pact.

The morning's light losses were also linked to some pre-weekend position squaring after a volatile week, although traders noted 10-year OLOs were holding up better than Bunds with the yield spread narrowing to seven basis points from eight

U.S. factory gate inflation data are forecast to show a mere 0.1 percent rise in both the headline PPI and the core, ex-food and ex-energy, PPI, confirming that price rises in the U.S. are under control and giving the view that U.S. interest rates are to remain stable for now a firmer base US-MCE.
"Benign figures are already factored in," a trader said.

Although U.S. players expect such data to attract capital flows out of Europe which they see struggling with EMU uncertainty, local players are seeing fewer and fewer reasons for pessimism that the single currency project will fail.

They said Friday's focus was on the French-German pre-Amsterdam summit talks, but with both parties keen on reaching an agreement and finding a solution for France's objections to the stability pact no bad news was expected.
"Only a failure will have an impact on the market," a trader said, "that would make German paper more attractive vis a vis southern European bonds."

A collapse of EMU would spark a selloff of Italian and Spanish bonds and spread widening over Bunds, he said. It was unclear how OLOs would fare in that scenario since Belgium's equally large state debt might outweigh the franc's link to the mark and be used as an excuse to offload OLOs too.
The market was, however, not working on that assumption.

"OLOs remain driven by Bunds," an analyst said, "the only attraction is the steepness of the yield curve. With the short end suggesting no rate hikes, performance will have to come from curve flattening i.e. steady, low-inflation economic data."

"With the prospect of a broad EMU (with Italy and Spain) the chances of this will be limited, so we will see range-trading," he added, forecasting the OLO/Bund spread would stay in its recent 5-15 basis point range.
